Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the recent call. We're close on the DPA but legal asked us to confirm a couple of transfer and subprocessor items before signature:

- Confirmation that Redwood will execute the EU SCCs (current European Commission clauses) as incorporated into the DPA.
- For UK transfers, our legal team prefers the UK IDTA / addendum language rather than a separate data transfer agreement; can you confirm Redwood can sign the standard UK IDTA addendum?
- We need the latest subprocessors list and a short Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) paragraph describing where data may transit and any safeguards (e.g., encryption, access controls, KMS regions).

I've attached our redline and the SCCs extract. If you can get a consolidated redline back this week, we can route for signature. We typically use DocuSign for execution.

Attachments: Acme_DPA_redline_20251103.docx, SCCs-extract.pdf

Best,

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood DPA — a few final points (SCCs / UK IDTA)

Thanks for the ping. I reviewed Acme's redline and prepared a consolidated Redwood response. High-level: we can accept incorporation of the EU SCCs and execute the standard UK IDTA addendum with one registration note (we'll record the execution in our contract register). Key redlines I left:

- Subprocessors: we keep the standard notice-and-objection flow and will provide the current list as an attachment. We will add language committing to notify Acme 30 days before adding new subprocessors that process personal data.
- TIA: added a short paragraph in the addendum that describes typical transfer paths (EU -> US for control plane logs; model inference may route through EU and US GPUs depending on region and model selection), and the safeguards (AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, role-based access controls, KMS with customer region support where applicable).
- No changes to our breach notification timeframes (we keep 72 hours for incidents affecting personal data), but clarified escalation points.

I've attached: Redwood_DPA_Redline_20251103.docx and IDTA-addendum-draft.docx. I recommend we offer DocuSign for execution (industry standard) — AdobeSign acceptable but DocuSign is what Acme suggested.

If you want, Aditya can provide a one-paragraph TIA summary we can include in the addendum header; that'll keep things tidy for Acme.

—Laura
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood DPA — a few final points (SCCs / UK IDTA)

Thanks Laura — happy to draft a concise TIA paragraph. Suggested wording below, feel free to adapt: 

"Transfer Impact Summary: Customer data is stored and processed primarily in the EU region for EU customers. Requests may be routed to dedicated inference capacity in other regions (including the US) depending on customer configuration and model selection. Redwood implements industry-standard safeguards: encryption at rest (AES-256), encryption in transit (TLS 1.2+), strict role-based access controls, and customer-managed keys where requested. We maintain subprocessors under contractual obligation to adhere to the SCCs/IDTA requirements and provide a subprocessors list on request."

I'll send that to Laura as a draft to paste into the addendum. On execution: DocuSign link is easiest. We should also include the subprocessors CSV as a supplemental attachment in the envelope.

—Aditya
VP, Product Operations | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com
